userBindings.summary: User rebinds live in keybindings.json (JSONC array) in the user folder, one per profile. Rules are appended after the defaults and evaluated bottom-up, so a user rule for the same key wins; a rule whose command starts with '-' removes a default.

locations.note: Default profile. Absent on this PC (read-only existence probe, S7): the user has no rebinds yet.
Per-profile keybindings when a non-default profile is active (S8). No profiles here.
Portable mode (a 'data' folder next to Code.exe).

userBindings.entryShape: Array of { "key": "ctrl+shift+alt+k", "command": "<command id>", "when"?: "<context expr>", "args"?: any, "systemWide"?: true }. 'command' is the join key (= verb.appAction). A leading '-' on command removes the default for that key (and when, if given); an empty command "" disables the key. Chords are two key strings separated by a space ("ctrl+k ctrl+s"). Comments and trailing commas are allowed (JSONC).
userBindings.keyNameMap: Lower-case, '+' between parts, any modifier order: ctrl, shift, alt, win (meta on Linux, cmd on macOS) -> Prism Win/Ctrl/Alt/Shift in canonical order. Keys: a-z, 0-9 and f1-f19 map 1:1 (upper-cased); left/up/right/down -> Left/Up/Right/Down; pageup/pagedown/home/end/insert/delete/tab/enter/space/backspace -> PageUp/PageDown/Home/End/Insert/Delete/Tab/Enter/Space/Backspace; escape -> Esc; pausebreak -> Pause; capslock -> CapsLock; ` -> Backquote, - -> Minus, = -> Equal, [ -> BracketLeft, ] -> BracketRight, \ -> Backslash, ; -> Semicolon, ' -> Quote, , -> Comma, . -> Period, / -> Slash; numpad0-9 -> Numpad0-9, numpad_add/_subtract/_multiply/_divide/_decimal -> NumpadAdd/NumpadSubtract/NumpadMultiply/NumpadDivide/NumpadDecimal; numpad_separator has no Prism name (keep unbound). Legacy VK names oem_1..oem_8 / oem_plus / oem_comma / oem_minus / oem_period / oem_102 -> Semicolon, Slash, Backquote, BracketLeft, Backslash, BracketRight, Quote, (oem_8: none), Equal, Comma, Minus, Period, IntlBackslash. Scan-code form in brackets ([KeyA], [Digit1], [Slash], [ArrowLeft], [Numpad0], [NumpadComma] …) names the physical US position: send it as a scancode for that one chord, not a VK. A space splits a chord sequence -> binding kind 'sequence'.
userBindings.readMode: Read-only. Strip // and /* */ comments and trailing commas, parse, watch the file (VS Code itself watches it). Apply in order: for each verb, the last user rule with command == appAction (and a when clause that is empty or compatible with the verb's context) replaces the default chord; a '-appAction' rule with no replacement marks the verb unbound. If the file doesn't parse, keep the defaults and say so in the PI. Use the active profile's file when the companion extension reports a non-default profile.

layouts.rationale: Palette, file jump and save on top; format/comment/quick fix and search/rename/chat in the middle; terminal, Git and debug at the bottom; tabs and scroll on layer 0 of the dials, problems and zoom on layer 1.
The debug toolbar becomes the top two rows in VS Code's own order (continue, over, into / out, restart, stop); breakpoints and the console below; the left dial steps through code.
Only keys the terminal doesn't pass to the shell: new/split/interrupt on top, history/clear/AI in the middle, build/debug/kill, then the way back to the editor; dials switch terminals and scroll.
Review flow: stage or revert the hunk on top, list/SCM/commit in the middle, push at the bottom; the left dial walks hunks and its push stages the current one.
Same zones as the editor page; the right column swaps quick fix and debug for the two preview keys, and the fold dial replaces problems for long documents.
Primary verbs on the top row, terminal/Git/fix/debug below; the four dials are tabs, scroll, problems and zoom with their readouts on the strip.
The four step keys across the top in toolbar order, session control below; dial 0 steps, the rest navigate.
Terminal actions on top, clear/AI/back-to-editor below; dials switch terminals, jump between commands and scroll.

conflicts: Terminal scroll: the Windows PDF (S3) lists Ctrl+Up/Down; 1.141.2 (S4) binds those to scroll-to-previous/next-command in the terminal and line scroll to Ctrl+Alt+PageUp/PageDown.
Ctrl+Shift+F: the docs (S2) list workbench.view.search; in 1.141.2 (S4) that rule never matches and workbench.action.findInFiles owns the key.
Ctrl+Shift+V: the PDF (S3) says 'Open Markdown preview'; the bundled extension (S5) binds markdown.togglePreview.
Ctrl+K Ctrl+R: core opens the Keyboard Shortcuts Reference (S4); the Git extension (S5) binds the same chord to Revert Selected Ranges in file editors.
Ctrl+I: inline chat (S4, S2) vs the secondary Trigger Suggest key (S3, S4); inline chat wins while chat is enabled.
Inline suggestion trigger: many guides say Alt+\ (old Copilot extension); 1.141.2 core and the bundled copilot 0.69.0 (S4, S5) have no default.
Machine-extracted summaries of S2 report Linux keys (Ctrl+Shift+I format, Ctrl+Alt+- back, Ctrl+Shift+A block comment); S4 and S3 agree on the Windows keys used here.
gaps: Terminal-focus and debug-session contexts need the planned Prism VS Code companion extension (or the opt-in ${focusedView} window title); until then use engine-tracked contexts.

notes: keyboard.dispatch is unset here (default 'code'): VS Code matches on KeyboardEvent.code, so VK injection lands on the same physical keys on a US layout. On other layouts, VS Code renders the chords per layout; send VKs for letters and use the scancode form only for [Key]-style user rules.

Keys for commands outside terminal.integrated.commandsToSkipShell go to the shell when the terminal is focused; verbs marked '*' or 'terminal' are all in that list (or are chords, which always skip the shell).
